solution: The 'Anti-liquor movement' section opens: "In 1992, in Andhra Pradesh, a movement was started against the drinking of alcohol. It received a good response in other States too." The chapter then details the anti-arrack movement and the Dubuganta village (Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh) incident of 1992. Maharashtra is a tempting rival because most of the chapter's other women's organisations are Maharashtrian, but the chapter places the anti-liquor movement's origin squarely in Andhra Pradesh and says it only spread elsewhere.

Under 'International Women's Year' the chapter says: "In 1975, the government of India constituted the Committee on the Status of Women and appointed Dr Phulrenu Guha as its Chairman." Pramila Dandavate is the tempting rival, but the chapter credits her with establishing the Mahila Dakshata Samiti in Delhi in 1976; Uma Bharati and Vasundhara Raje appear only in the 'Women Chief Ministers in India' box.
